definition: Terms/codes for describing the clinical signs, symptoms and conditions of the affected person appearing as a result of the medical device adverse event/incident
statusDescription: Please use more detailed term within the hierarchy

definition: Nervous System
statusDescription: Please use more detailed term within the hierarchy

definition: A feeling of falling down which can occur whether the person is standing, sitting or lying down.
Damage to the brain.
Hernia of brain substance and meninges through a congenital or traumatic opening of the skull.
A swelling in the brain caused by the presence of excessive fluid.
Unexpected increase in cerebral blood flow after carotid endarterectomy (CEA) or carotid artery stenting (CAS).
Abnormal enlargement of the cerebral ventricles.
statusDescription: Term was modified on 21 January 2021 (old term: Cerebral Ventriculomeglia).

definition: The loss of cerebrospinal fluid into the surrounding tissues or outside the body.
statusDescription: Definition modified for Release Number 2024. See no. 6 of Change Log

definition: Changes in perception, thinking, or remembering.
A mental state characterized by a lack of clear and orderly thought and behavior.
Loss of intellectual abilities interfering with an individual's social and occupational functions.
Traumatic brain injury as a result of the action of a mechanical force on the head.
Sudden, involuntary skeletal muscular contractions of cerebral or brain stem origin.
A convulsion marked by alternating contracting and relaxing of the muscles.
A convulsion marked by prolonged contraction of the muscles.
Epilepsy caused or apparently caused by device. Do not use when epilepsy is a pre-existing condition.
A life-threatening condition characterised by a single prolonged seizure or a series of seizures without intervening full recovery of consciousness.
statusDescription: Editorial change to the definition on 16 February 2021.

definition: Decreased sensitivity affecting one or more senses
statusDescription: Term and Definition modified for Release Number 2025. Previous term was "Decreased Sensitivity". See no. 115 of Change Request Log. Editorial change to term for Release Number 2026. See no. 251 of Change Log.

definition: Increased sensitivity affecting one or more senses
statusDescription: Term and Definition modified for Release Number 2025. Previous term was "Increased Sensitivity". See no. 119 of Change Request Log. Editorial change to term for Release Number 2026. See no. 252 of Change Log.

definition: A sensation of lightheadedness, unsteadiness, turning, spinning or rocking.
Impairment of verbal communication skills, often resulting from brain damage.
Inability to speak.
An acute inflammatory process affecting the brain parenchyma.
A functional and/or structural disorder of the brain that is acquired or congenital and characterised by mental and neurological symptoms.
statusDescription: Editorial change to the definition on 16 February 2021.

definition: Pain in various parts of the head, not confined to the area of distribution of any nerve.
A disorder characterized by an abnormal increase of cerebrospinal fluid in the ventricles of the brain.
Bleeding within the cranium.
A level of awareness that can be described as consistently not responsive to stimuli.
statusDescription: Editorial change to term for Release Number 2026. See no. 253 of Change Log.

definition: A state of profound unconsciousness associated with markedly depressed cerebral activity.
Extremely weak; threatened with syncope.
A spontaneous, transient, loss of consciousness caused by insufficient blood supply to the brain.
Systematic and extensive loss or impairment of memory caused by organic or psychological factors. This may be temporary or permanent, and may involve old or recent memories.
A disorder characterized by acute inflammation of the meninges of the brain and/or spinal cord.
Neurological conditions resulting in abnormal voluntary or involuntary movement, which may impact the speed, fluency, quality and ease of movement.
Difficulty moving; distortion or impairment of voluntary movement, as in tic, spasm, or myoclonus.
Partial or complete loss of function of one or more muscles. It is usually caused by damage to the nervous system.
Paralysis of the legs and lower part of the body.
A slight or incomplete paralysis.
Paralysis of all four limbs.
The shaking movement of the whole body or just a certain part of it, often caused by problems of the neurons responsible for muscle action.
The occurrence of a single contraction or a series of contractions of a muscle.
A condition that is characterized by an irresistible urgency to move the legs to obtain relief from a strange and uncomfortable sensation in the legs.
statusDescription: Term was added on 27 January 2022. For details, see comment No. 85 of the Change Log (Release Number 2022).

definition: A partial or complete loss of function of one or more of the facial muscles resulting in paralysis of the facial regions. Includes both central and peripheral facial paralysis or palsy.
statusDescription: Term was added on 27 January 2022. For details, see comment No. 242 / 243 / 244 / 245 of the Change Log (Release Number 2022).

definition: Movement disorder characterized by involuntary muscle contractions.
statusDescription: New term added for Release Number 2026. See no.112 of Change Request Log.

definition: Inability to perform particular purposive actions
statusDescription: New term added for Release Number 2026. See no.113 of Change Request Log.

definition: Injury to nervous tissue.
Injury to optical nerve.
Injury to the central or peripheral nervous system.
Traumatic damage of the spinal cord.
Intense painful sensation along a nerve or group of nerves.
A disorder affecting the cranial nerves or the peripheral nervous system. It manifests with pain, tingling, numbness, and muscle weakness.
The loss of the sensation of feeling in an area of the body.
Injury to the peripheral nervous system.
Pain or discomfort caused by exposure of the dentin layer of tooth to thermal, tactile, or other stimuli.
A change from the patient's baseline sleeping pattern, in the hours slept and/or an alteration/dysfunction in the stages of sleep.
A term referring to disorders characterized by the disruption of normal speech. It includes stuttering, lisps, dysarthria and voice disorders.
A chronic adhesive arachnoiditis in the spinal arachnoid, with root and spinal cord symptoms similar to those caused by pressure from a tumor.
A sudden loss of neurological function secondary to hemorrhage or ischemia in the brain parenchyma due to a vascular event.
An acute neurological deficit caused by bleeding within the brain or between the brain and the skull.
An ischemic condition of the brain, producing a persistent focal neurological deficit in the area of distribution of the cerebral arteries.
conditions characterized by an alteration in the ability to or perception of touch.
Increased sensitivity to tactile stimulation.
Impairment of tactile sensitivity manifesting as partial loss of sensitivity to sensory stimuli.
Abnormal touch sensations, such as burning or prickling, that occur without an outside stimulus.
Conditions characterized by an alteration in taste function or perception
statusDescription: Editorial change to the definition on 16 February 2021.

definition: Inability to taste.
Distortion of taste.
An involuntary, compulsive, repetitive stereotyped movement.
A brief attack (from a few minutes to an hour) of cerebral dysfunction of vascular origin, with no persistent neurological deficit.
Unintended reaction in nerve system caused by electrical stimulation.
statusDescription: Term retired for Release Number 2025. Use E2131 - Inappropriate Device Stimulation of Tissue. See no. 17 of Change Request Log

definition: The report describes a non-specific problem with the nervous system. Note: Please use E2402 if the report describes a specific injury but the relevant term does not exist.
statusDescription: Term was added on 18 March 2020 for cases where the category of a health effect was reported but with no further details. Editorial change to definition for Release Number 2026. See no. 196 of Change Log.

definition: Pressure within the craniospinal compartment is increased.
statusDescription: Term was added on 27 January 2022. For details, see comment No. 86 of the Change Log (Release Number 2022).

definition: The presence of air or gas within the cranial cavity.
statusDescription: Term was added on 27 January 2022. For details, see comment No. 212 of the Change Log (Release Number 2022).

definition: A condition that mimics the presence of a tumor (Pseudotumour Cerebri) or hydrocephalus, caused by chronic  increase in intracranial pressure.
statusDescription: Term was added on 27 January 2022. For details, see comment No. 219 of the Change Log (Release Number 2022). Editorial change to definition for Release Number 2026. See no. 186 of Change Log.

definition: A level of awareness and arousal other than normal.
statusDescription: Term was added on 27 January 2022. For details, see comment No. 77 of the Change Log (Release Number 2022).

definition: A neurological state characterised by increased ability to perceive and respond.
statusDescription: Term was added on 27 January 2022. For details, see comment No. 77 of the Change Log (Release Number 2022).

definition: A neurological state characterised by decreased ability to perceive and respond.
statusDescription: Term was added on 27 January 2022. For details, see comment No. 77 of the Change Log (Release Number 2022).

definition: Injury to the dura mater, with or without damage to any other layer of the meninges.
statusDescription: Term added for Release Number 2024. See no. 22 of Change Log

definition: Conditions characterized by an alteration in the function or perception of smell, including diminished, distorted, or lost olfactory sensation.
statusDescription: Term added for Release Number 2026. See no. 111 of Change Log.

definition: Diminished or absent reflex responses
statusDescription: Term added for Release Number 2026. See no. 14 of Change Log.

definition: Mental, Emotional and Behavioral Disorders
statusDescription: Please use more detailed term within the hierarchy. Editorial amendment to term and definition for Release Number 2026. See no. 187 of Change Log.

definition: Excessive clenching of the jaw and grinding of the teeth.
Change from the affected person's usual emotional state.
Apprehension or uneasiness which may be accompanied by restlessness, tension, tachycardia, and dyspnea.
A condition marked by ongoing feelings of sadness, despair, loss of energy, diminished interest/pleasure and difficulty dealing with normal daily life.
A state of physiological or psychological stress that cannot be compensated for by normal adaptive measures.
A feeling of general discomfort or uneasiness, an out-of-sorts feeling.
A feeling of agitation. Tending to become frustrated or upset easily.
A false sensory perception in the absence of an external stimulus.
Characterized by a lack of vitality or energy.
Thoughts of taking one's own life.

term: Unspecified Mental, Emotional or Behavioral Problem
definition: The report describes a non-specific Mental, Emotional or Behavioral problem. Note: Please use E2402 if the report describes a specific problem but the relevant term does not exist.
statusDescription: Term was added on 18 March 2020 for cases where the category of a health effect was reported but with no further details. Editorial changes to term and definition for Release Number 2026. See no. 188 and 197 of Change Log.

definition: A usually reversible condition characterized by the acute and sudden development of confusion, illusions, movement changes, inattentiveness, agitation and hallucinations.
statusDescription: Term was added on 27 January 2022. For details, see comment No. 36 of the Change Log (Release Number 2022).

definition: A mental disorder characterized by personality change, impaired functioning and loss of touch with reality.
statusDescription: Term was added on 27 January 2022. For details, see comment No. 37 of the Change Log (Release Number 2022).

definition: The sensation of struggling to remain awake.
statusDescription: Term was added on 31 January 2023. For details, see comment No. 77 of the Change Log (Release Number 2023).

definition: Excessive mistrust or suspicion of people -thinking incorrectly, for example, that someone is trying to hurt you, that people are doing things to deliberately annoy you or that there is a conspiracy against you.
statusDescription: Term added for Release Number 2026. See no. 65 of Change Log.

definition: Blood and Lymphatic System
statusDescription: Please use more detailed term within the hierarchy

definition: A reduction in the number of red blood cells, the amount of hemoglobin, and/or the volume of packed red blood cells.
Anemia resulting from the premature destruction of the peripheral blood red cells.
A condition in which there is a deviation from or interruption of the normal coagulation properties of the blood.
A pathological process where the blood starts to coagulate throughout the whole body. This depletes the body of its platelets and coagulation factors, and there is an increased risk of hemorrhage.
Low blood platelet count.
Disruption of the integrity of the erythrocyte membrane causing release of hemoglobin.
An abnormally high circulating blood volume.
statusDescription: Definition was modified on 21 January 2021 (Old definition: Too much fluid in the blood.). For details, see comment No. 2 of the Change Log.

definition: An abnormally low circulating blood volume.

The presence of pathogenic microorganisms in the blood stream causing a rapidly progressing systemic reaction that may lead to shock. Symptoms include fever, chills, tachycardia, and increased respiratory rate. It is a medical emergency that requires urgent medical attention.
A tumor-like collection of serum in the tissues.
The presence of an enlarged lymph node.
The white blood cell count is below the normal range, including neutropenia.
statusDescription: Definition was modified on 27 January 2022 (Old definition:The white blood cell count is below the normal range.). MedDRA mapping also updated from White blood cell count decreased (10047942) to White blood cell count low (10051617). For details, see comment No. 73 of the Change Log (Release Number 2022).

definition: The report describes a non-specific problem with the blood or lymphatic system. Note: Please use E2402 if the report describes a specific problem but the relevant term does not exist.
statusDescription: Term was added on 18 March 2020 for cases where the category of a health effect was reported but with no further details. Term and definition modified for Release Number 2026. See no. 198 and 254 of Change log.

definition: The white blood cell count is above the normal range.
statusDescription: Term was added on 27 January 2022. For details, see comment No. 79 of the Change Log (Release Number 2022).

definition: Adverse events associated with the transfusion of whole blood or one of its components, most commonly a hemolytic reaction to cross-typed blood.
statusDescription: Term was added on 27 January 2022. For details, see comment No. 202 of the Change Log (Release Number 2022).

definition: One or more of the blood protein levels being higher or lower than normal (e.g. Albumin, C-reactive Protein).
statusDescription: Term was added on 27 January 2022. For details, see comment No. 108 / 111 of the Change Log (Release Number 2022).

definition: Immune System
statusDescription: Please use more detailed term within the hierarchy

definition: A disorder resulting from loss of function or tissue destruction of an organ or multiple organs, arising from humoral or cellular immune responses of the individual to his own tissue constituents.
A local or general reaction of an organism following contact with a specific allergen to which it has been previously exposed and to which it has become sensitized.
statusDescription: Editorial change to term for Release Number 2026. See no. 255 of Change Log.

definition: Progression of anaphylaxis into systemic shock, which is characterized by significant reduction in tissue perfusion which leads to hypoxia and hypotension, and can lead to death if untreated.
Acute immune response that occurs from exposure to an allergen. For conditions which have progressed to systemic shock, use E040201 - Anaphylactic Shock.
statusDescription: Definition was modified on 31 January 2023 (Old definition: Resembling anaphylaxis.) MedDRA mapping also updated from Anaphylactoid reaction (10002216) to Anaphylaxis (10002218). For details, see comment No. 78 of the Change Log (Release Number 2023).

definition: A regionally-limited response to an antigen, which may include inflammation, induration, erythema, pruritus or pain.
A deficiency of immune response or a disorder characterized by deficient immune response.

Indicates that antibodies directed against nuclear antigens have been detected. Almost invariably found in systemic lupus erythematosus and are frequently found in rheumatoid arthritis, scleroderma, Sjogren's Syndrome and mixed connective tissue disease.
statusDescription: Editorial change to term for Release Number 2026. See no. 256 of Change Log.

definition: The report describes a non-specific problem with the immune system. Note: Please use E2402 if the report describes a specific problem but the relevant term does not exist.
statusDescription: Term was added on 18 March 2020 for cases where the category of a health effect was reported but with no further details. Editorial change to definition for Release Number 2026. See no. 199 of Change Log.

definition: Vascular System
statusDescription: Please use more detailed term within the hierarchy

definition: Bulging or ballooning in an area of an artery secondary to arterial wall weakening.
An aneurysm that has burst, resulting in hemorrhage into adjacent tissues.
Expansion of aneurysm.
statusDescription: Term was added on 27 January 2022. For details, see comment No. 185 of the Change Log (Release Number 2022). Editorial change to term for Release Number 2026. See no. 257 of Release Log.

definition: A vascular disorder characterized by thickening and hardening of the walls of the arteries. Build-up of fatty material and calcium deposition in the arterial wall resulting in partial or complete occlusion of the arterial lumen.
The blockage of a blood vessel lumen by air or solid material such as blood clot or other tissues (e.g., adipose tissue, cancer cells) that have migrated from another anatomic site.
The presence of bubbles of air in the vascular system; occurrence is related to the entry of air into the venous circulation following trauma or surgery.
Type of embolism when lumen of vessel or ductus is occluded by part of device.
The obstruction of the pulmonary artery or one of its branches by an embolus, sometimes associated with infarction of the lung.
Occlusion of the lumen of a vessel by a thrombus that has migrated from a distal site via the blood stream.
The blockage of a blood vessel by fat particles in the circulation.
statusDescription: Term added for Release Number 2024. See no. 57 of Change Log. Editorial change to term for Release Number 2026. See no. 258 of Release Log.

definition: The leakage of body fluid or cells from the vascular system to the surrounding tissues. This process occurs either by force or as a result of a pathologic reaction (e.g., inflammation).
A localized collection of blood, usually clotted, in an organ, space, or tissue, due to a break in the wall of a blood vessel.
The loss of blood from the circulation, including blood loss from a device connected to a patient.
statusDescription: Term and definition was modified on 27 January 2022 (Old term/definition: Hemorrhage/Bleeding: The loss of blood from a ruptured blood vessel.). For details, see comment No. 87 / 199 of the Change Log (Release Number 2022).

definition: A flat discoloration of the skin or a mucous membrane, larger in area than a petechia, caused by the extravasation of blood. Discolouration under the skin caused by a bleed underneath. Typically a bruise.
Extensive loss of blood due to internal or external hemorrhage.
The measurement of the mean left atrial pressure, as measured by a catheter introduced into the distal pulmonary artery, is high.
The measurement of the mean left atrial pressure, as measured by a catheter introduced into the distal pulmonary artery, is low.
statusDescription: Definition was modified on 21 January 2021 (Old definition: The measurement of the mean left pulmonary atrial pressure, as measured by a catheter introduced into the distal pulmonary artery, is low.). For details, see comment No. 3 of the Change Log.

definition: Lack of oxygen in tissues, commonly due to impaired blood supply to an area of the body, resulting in impairment of tissue oxygenation.
The formation of new blood vessels.
Damage to a blood vessel resulting from a full thickness disruption in the integrity of the vessel wall.
Damage to the venae cavae, pulmonary artery, pulmonary veins or aorta resulting from a full thickness disruption in the integrity of the vessel wall.
Inflammation of any one of the blood vessels, including the arteries, veins, and rest of the vasculature system in the body.
statusDescription: Term and Definition and MedDRA map modified for Release Number 2024. Previous term was Phlebitis. Previous MedDRA map was 10034879:Phlebitis. See no. 19 of Change Log. Editorial change to definition for Release Number 2026. See no. 175 of Release Log.

definition: The creation of hematoma outside the arterial wall following bleeding due to puncture of the arterial wall. Pseudoaneurysms can also occur in the heart chambers following myocardial infarction with rupture of the wall of the ventricle.
The formation of a blood clot in the lumen of a vessel or heart chamber.
Spontaneous or induced tear within the wall of a blood vessel.
Spontaneous or induced tear within the wall of the aorta
statusDescription: Term added for Release Number 2024. See no. 83 of Change Log. Editorial change to term for Release Number 2026. See no. 259 of Release Log.

definition: Vasoconstriction involves narrowing of a blood vessel lumen due to smooth muscle contraction in the vessel wall and leads to decreased blood flow.
Widening of a blood vessel lumen due to smooth muscle relaxation in the vessel wall and leads to increased blood flow.
The report describes a non-specific problem with the vascular system. Note: Please use E2402 if the report describes a specific problem but the relevant term does not exist.
statusDescription: Term was added on 18 March 2020 for cases where the category of a health effect was reported but with no further details. Editorial change to definition for Release Number 2026. See no. 200 of Release Log.

definition: Inadequate blood flow to a particular area of the body.
statusDescription: Term was added on 27 January 2022. For details, see comment No. 190 of the Change Log (Release Number 2022).

definition: Tissue damage caused when blood supply returns to tissue after a period of ischemia or lack of oxygen. The restoration of circulation results in inflammation and oxidative damage.
statusDescription: Term was added on 31 January 2023. For details, see comment No. 125 of the Change Log (Release Number 2023).

definition: Partial or total occlusion or obstruction of the coronary ostia or artery.
statusDescription: Term added for Release Number 2024. See no. 82 of Change Log. Editorial change to term for Release Number 2026. See no. 260 of Release Log.

definition: Contraction of muscular walls of blood vessels
statusDescription: Term added for Release Number 2025. See no. 35 of Change Log

definition: Persistent blood flow in the false lumen of a dissection following an endovascular aortic repair (EVAR) procedure.
nonImdrfMappings: MedDRA:10074841:Continued perfusion of a false lumen
statusDescription: Term added for Release Number 2025. See no. 66 of Change Log

definition: A condition characterized by abnormally low systemic vascular resistance, often presenting with hypotension and preserved or elevated cardiac output; may be referred to as vasodilatory shock or vascular tone loss
statusDescription: Term added for Release Number 2026. See no. 17 of Change Log

definition: A deviation from normal central venous pressure values
statusDescription: Term added for Release Number 2026. See no. 26 of Change Log

definition: Telangiectasia, also known as Spider veins or thread veins, are prominent clusters of small, damaged blood vessels visible in the skin. They appear as thin red, blue, or purple lines.
statusDescription: Term added for Release Number 2026. See no. 67 of Change Log

definition: Heart
statusDescription: Please use more detailed term within the hierarchy

definition: Any variation from the normal rate or rhythm (which may include the origin of the impulse and/or its subsequent propagation) in the heart.
An electrocardiographic finding showing a state of cardiac standstill with no cardiac output and no ventricular depolarization.
Irregular heart rhythm, usually associated with a rapid rate, that is caused by abnormal electrical activity within the atrial.
A rapid heart rate, associated with a regular rhythm, that is caused by abnormal electrical activity within the atria.
An abnormally slow heart rate. Thresholds for different age, gender, and patient populations exist.
A cardiac beat originating from an abnormal site. These changes lead to extra or dropped heartbeats.
An interference with the normal conduction of electrical impulses that control activity of the heart muscle.
An electrocardiographic finding of three or more consecutive complexes of ventricular origin. The QRS complexes are wide and have an abnormal morphology. (CDISC)
A pulse that beats at irregular intervals.
Abnormally high heart rate. Thresholds for different age, gender, and patient populations exist.
Arrhythmia characterized by chaotic contractions of the ventricular muscle.
The sudden cessation of productive cardiac activity in an individual who becomes unresponsive, without normal breathing and no signs of circulation.
Increase from the normal levels of cardiac enzymes.
The presence of an acquired hole in the heart.

Acute compression of the heart caused by increased intrapericardial pressure due to the accumulation of blood or fluid in the pericardium from rupture of the heart or great vessels, penetrating trauma, or progressive effusion.
A disease of the heart muscle.
Circulatory dysfunction/insufficiency due to a decrease in the force of the cardiac contractions and / or the tone of the vascular walls. Includes diastolic and systolic dysfunction.
statusDescription:
Term and definition was modified on 31 January 2023 (Old term/definition: Cardiovascular Insufficiency: Circulatory insufficiency due to a decrease in the force of the cardiac contractions and / or the tone of the vascular walls.). For details, see comment No. 81 of the Change Log (Release Number 2023).

definition: A tear located on a leaflet of a heart valve that prevents its complete closing, which can result in valvular dysfunction.
Weak or absent palpable pulse due to decreased arterial pulse pressure.
Inflammation of the endocardium.
Inability of the heart to pump blood adequately to fill tissue metabolic requirements or the ability to do so only at an elevated filling pressure.

A disorder of cardiac function caused by insufficient blood flow to the muscle tissue of the heart. The decreased blood flow may be due to narrowing of the coronary arteries, to obstruction by a thrombus, or less commonly, to diffuse narrowing of arterioles and other small vessels within the heart. Severe interruption of the blood supply to the myocardial tissue may result in necrosis of cardiac muscle (myocardial infarction).
Chest pain resulting from inadequate oxygen delivery for the needs of the myocardium.
A condition which occurs when blood flow decreases or stops to a part of the heart, causing damage to the heart muscle.
A below normal volume of blood pumped from the right or left ventricle of the heart per unit time.
A rupture in the mitral valve tissue due to traumatic or pathologic processes.
A bruise to the heart.
Thickening of the myocardium often due to chronic pressure overload.
Inflammation of the muscle tissue of the heart.
An electrocardiographic finding of a change in cardiac electrical activity.
statusDescription: Editorial change to term for Release Number 2026. See no. 261 of Change Log.

definition: Fluid collection within the pericardial sac, usually due to inflammation.
statusDescription: Error in MedDRA mapping corrected for Release No. 2024

definition: Inflammation of the pericardium.
Dysfunction of one of the cardiac valves, with incomplete valve closure or damage to a valve leaflet resulting in valvular backflow.
Incomplete closure or damage to a valve leaflet of the aortic valve, resulting in aortic valve backflow.
Incomplete closure or damage to a valve leaflet of the mitral valve, resulting in mitral valve backflow.
Incomplete closure or damage to a valve leaflet of the pulmonary valve, resulting in pulmonary valve backflow.
Incomplete closure or damage to a valve leaflet of the tricuspid valve, resulting in tricuspid valve backflow.
Obstruction of flow across a heart valve due to immobility of the leaflets and/or a restricted orifice.
Obstruction of flow across a aortic heart valve due to immobility reduced elasticity of the leaflets and/or a restricted orifice.
Obstruction of flow across a mitral heart valve due to immobility reduced elasticity of the leaflets and/or a restricted orifice.
Obstruction of flow across a pulmonary heart valve due to immobility reduced elasticity of the leaflets and/or a restricted orifice.
Obstruction of flow across a tricuspid heart valve due to immobility reduced elasticity of the leaflets and/or a restricted orifice.
The report describes a non-specific problem with the heart. Note: Please use E2402 if the report describes a specific problem but the relevant term does not exist.
statusDescription: Term was added on 18 March 2020 for cases where the category of a health effect was reported but with no further details. Editorial change to definition for Release Number 2026. See no. 201 of Release Log.

definition: An intraoperative event that results in damage to, or abnormal function of, a heart valve. E.g. a tear in the leaflet or the chordae tendinae.
statusDescription: Term was added on 31 January 2023. For details, see comment No. 80 / 114 of the Change Log (Release Number 2023). Definition modified for Release Number 2025. See no. 62 of Change Request Log

definition: Irregular blood flow in the heart after surgical correction of a septal defect.
statusDescription: Term was added on 31 January 2023. For details, see comment No. 82 of the Change Log (Release Number 2023).

definition: Increased pressure across the heart valve
statusDescription: Term was added on 31 January 2023. For details, see comment No. 112 of the Change Log (Release Number 2023).

definition: An intraoperative event that results in damage to, or abnormal function of, the heart. For valvular injury, use E0624 - Intraoperative Cardiac Valve Injury
statusDescription: Term was added on 31 January 2023. For details, see comment No. 118 of the Change Log (Release Number 2023). Definition modified for Release Number 2025. See no. 62 of Change Request Log.

definition: A collection of air or gas in the pericardial cavity.
statusDescription: Term added for Release Number 2025. See no. 32 of Change Request Log

definition: The feeling of having a fast-beating, fluttering or pounding heart.
statusDescription: Term added for Release Number 2025. See no. 60 of Change Request Log

definition: Unusual physical findings on precordial examination, including palpable vibrations, thrills, or ventricular heaves.
statusDescription: Term added for Release Number 2026. See no.15 of Change Request Log

definition: Respiratory System
statusDescription: Please use more detailed term within the hierarchy

definition: Progressive and life-threatening pulmonary distress in the absence of an underlying pulmonary condition, usually following major trauma or surgery. Cases of neonatal respiratory distress syndrome are not included in this definition.
Blockage of air flow in the respiratory tract.
Transient cessation of respiration.
The entry of foreign material past the trachea, and into the lower respiratory tract.
Inflammation of the lungs due to the inhalation of solid or liquid material.
A chronic respiratory disease manifested as difficulty breathing due to the narrowing of bronchial passageways.
Bleeding from the bronchial wall and/or lung parenchyma.
An acute or chronic inflammatory process affecting the bronchi.
Sudden contraction of the smooth muscles of the bronchial wall.
Interference with respiration by obstruction of the larynx or trachea.
statusDescription: Editorial change to the definition on 16 February 2021.

definition: A chronic and progressive lung disorder characterized by the loss of elasticity of the bronchial tree and the air sacs, destruction of the air sacs wall, thickening of the bronchial wall, and mucous accumulation in the bronchial tree. The pathologic changes result in the disruption of the air flow in the bronchial airways. Signs and symptoms include shortness of breath, wheezing, productive cough, and chest tightness. The two main types of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease are chronic obstructive bronchitis and emphysema.
A condition characterized by increase beyond normal in the size of air spaces distal to the terminal bronchioles, either from dilatation of the alveoli or from destruction of their walls.
A sudden, often repetitive, spasmodic contraction of the thoracic cavity, resulting in violent release of air from the lungs, and usually accompanied by a distinctive sound.
Decrease in the maximum flow rate generated during a forceful exhalation, starting from full lung inflation.
statusDescription: Editorial change to term for Release Number 2026. See no. 262 of Change Log.

definition: An increase of the greatest rate of flow that can be achieved during forced expiration beginning with the lungs fully inflated.
statusDescription: Editorial change to term for Release Number 2026. See no. 263 of Change Log.

definition: Abnormal decrease of rate of breathing.
Abnormal increase of rate of breathing.
An uncomfortable sensation of difficulty breathing. It may present as an acute or chronic sign of an underlying respiratory or heart disorder.
Nose bleed.
A decrease in the fraction of the forced vital capacity that is exhaled in a specific number of seconds.
An increase in the fraction of the forced vital capacity that is exhaled in a specific number of seconds.
Coughing up blood from the respiratory tract.
A collection of blood in the pleural cavity.
An involuntary contraction of the diaphragm against closed vocal cords, producing the hic sound.
Abnormally prolonged, rapid, and deep breathing.
A state in which there is a reduced amount of air entering the pulmonary alveoli.
A deficiency in the amount of oxygen reaching the tissues.
Displacement of structures in the thoracic cavity in one direction due to increased pleural pressure on the contralateral side.
Blockage of the nasal passages.
Abnormal permanent enlargement of the lung air spaces distal to terminal bronchiole not resulted from wall destruction, e.g. due to loss of opposite lung.
Inflammation of the throat most often caused by viral and bacterial infections.
Increased amounts of fluid within the pleural cavity. Symptoms include shortness of breath, cough, and chest pain.
An accumulation of pus in the pleural space
An acute and/or chronic inflammation focally or diffusely affecting the lung parenchyma.
Acute inflammation of the walls of the terminal bronchioles.
Abnormal presence of air in the pleural cavity.
Impaired or abnormal functioning of the pulmonary system causing multiple pulmonary issues.
Accumulation of fluid in the lung tissues causing disturbance of the gas exchange that may lead to respiratory failure.
Increased pressure within the pulmonary circulation due to lung or heart disorder.
Localized necrosis of lung tissue caused by obstruction of the arterial blood supply, most often due to pulmonary embolism.
A condition in which the blood pH is less than normal, secondary to impaired gas exchange.
A condition in which the blood pH is greater than normal, secondary to impaired gas exchange.
Cessation of breathing function.
